newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude weak on prompt overhang after run cuts.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude weak on prompt overhang after run cuts.

text.p: North Sea crude oil fell on Tuesday as an overhang of early September barrels continued to weigh on premiums while speculators joined a sell-off of the IPE futures contract.
October Brent shed 27 cents from Friday's close to $20.14 per barrel, and the Sep/Oct spread lost 5 cents to +44 cents.
"All in all it's looking a bit weak. We've seen a fair correction in outright prices and premiums have followed suit," a major North Sea producer said.
Brent, Statfjord and Oseberg were the worst hit as offers tumbled to match refiners' lower valuations.

Last week's rise in outright Brent prices, which closed the arbitrage to the United States and ate into refining margins, was mostly to blame for the decline, traders said, but one saw hope for the second half of September.
Brent was on offer again having traded twice at September -15 cents over the past two days and Statfjord and Oseberg were offered at 20 and 15 cents over Dated Brent respectively.
Traders said the transatlantic arbitrage was still closed, but saw some hope for the second half of September.

There were rumours on the shipping market that Statoil was looking to fix a VLCC of Oseberg to the United States to shore up European prices and also that Sinochem fixed a VLCC of Norwegian crude to Rijeka on September 17-19.

"It's looking better in the second half. The refinery run cuts caused some overstocking in the first half, but that should be gone by the middle of the month and margins are already turning positive," a British-based refiner said.
